name: France
sub: Citeo's harmonised national sorting rules (Triman / Info-tri): all packaging and paper in the yellow bin since 2023, glass banks, and mandatory food-waste sorting since January 2024.

banana.w: Fruit peel is food waste, and since 2024 every household must sort it out via a brown bin or compost.

eggshell.w: Egg shells break down in compost and are accepted by food-waste collections.

coffee.w: Coffee grounds are ideal compost material; paper filters can go in with them.

bones.w: Most municipal food-waste bins take meat scraps and bones, but home compost can't break them down, so there they go in the grey bin.

shampoo.w: Plastic bottles are packaging; empty it and put it in the yellow bin with the cap on.

polybag.w: Since the extended sorting rules, all plastic packaging including bags and films goes in the yellow bin.

chips.w: Crisp packets are packaging, so under the extended rules they go in the yellow bin.

tube.w: Toothpaste tubes are packaging; the national rules accept them in the yellow bin, no need to clean.

carton.w: Drink cartons are recycled for their paper fibres and go in the yellow bin, emptied and flattened.

eggtray.w: It's cardboard packaging for the yellow bin; moulded pulp can also be composted.

box.w: Flattened cardboard goes in the yellow bin; very large boxes go to the recycling centre.

pizza.w: Emptied pizza boxes go in the yellow bin, but some areas ask for greasy or food-soaked parts to go in the grey bin.

newspaper.w: All paper goes in the yellow bin in most areas, though some towns still have a separate paper bank.

jar.w: Glass jars are packaging glass; put them in the bottle bank and the metal lid in the yellow bin.

wine.w: Glass bottles go in the glass bank and are recycled into new bottles endlessly.

perfume.w: A glass perfume bottle is packaging glass, so it goes in the glass bank.

tin.w: Steel and aluminium food tins go in the yellow bin; metal is sorted out magnetically and recycled.

window.w: Window glass melts at a different temperature from bottle glass, so take it to the recycling centre, not the glass bank.

drinkglass.w: Drinking glasses have a different composition from bottle glass and would spoil a recycling batch, so wrap it and bin it.

mirror.w: Mirror glass is coated and can't go in the glass bank; take it to the recycling centre or wrap small pieces for the grey bin.

tissue.w: Used tissues can't be recycled; they go in the grey bin, though many food-waste collections also accept them.

diaper.w: Nappies mix plastic, pulp and waste, so they can't be recycled and go in the grey bin.

pad.w: Sanitary products are hygiene waste and go in the grey bin, never the toilet.

battery.w: Batteries contain metals that can be recovered; every shop selling them has a free drop-off box.

bulb.w: Energy-saving bulbs contain a little mercury, so take them to a shop collection box or recycling centre.

meds.w: Take unused medicines to any pharmacy for safe destruction; the empty cardboard box goes in the yellow bin.

paint.w: Leftover paint is hazardous waste and goes to the recycling centre or a paint-shop take-back point.

toy.w: Toys aren't packaging, so they don't go in the yellow bin; small broken toys go in the grey bin, larger ones to the recycling centre.
